prompt: Stage 3-2, level 6, 31 gold. Your 1-cost ranged carry is already 2-star and holds your item. The shop shows another copy for 1 gold and your bench has two free slots. Do you buy it?

options.label: No: a fourth copy does nothing on its own, a 3-star needs nine, and the bench slot is worth more
Yes: every copy is progress toward the 3-star
Yes, and refresh to look for more copies while they are cheap

explanation:
Three copies make a 2-star and nine make a 3-star. A fourth copy is not an upgrade of any kind: it sits on the bench until five more arrive, and at level 6 only 30% of shop slots are 1-costs, so 'five more' is a lot of rounds and gold. A 3-star 1-cost is a real plan for some boards, but one you choose on purpose with a full bench of copies, not something you drift into 1 gold at a time.

Refreshing to hunt more copies is the expensive version of the same mistake: 2 gold a spin at 3-2, when you should be climbing toward 50.
principle: Copies matter at three and at nine; the ones in between are bench space until you decide to go for the 3-star.
commonMistake: Buying stray fourth and fifth copies 'for the 3-star' with no intention of rolling for it.
hint: Count how many more copies the next upgrade needs, and how often a 1-cost appears in your shop at this level.
